questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which symptom cluster is most consistent with acute pyelonephritis rather than bladder-only cystitis?
choices: Isolated urgency without systemic symptoms
Fever, chills, flank pain, and nausea
Painless bacteriuria without urinary symptoms
Chronic nocturia without a new change
questions.explanation: Fever, flank or costovertebral-angle pain, chills, and nausea suggest upper urinary-tract involvement and require assessment for severity and complications.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: A catheterized adult feels well and has no fever, flank pain, suprapubic pain, or systemic illness, but a urine culture grows bacteria. What is the best interpretation?
choices: The result alone proves CAUTI requiring antibiotics
Bacteriuria may represent colonization; assess symptoms and indications before treating
The catheter must be changed daily
Every positive culture means kidney infection
questions.explanation: Bacteriuria is common with indwelling catheters. Without symptoms or systemic signs, it often represents asymptomatic bacteriuria rather than a treatable CAUTI.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: An older adult has new confusion and bacteria in urine but no urinary symptoms, fever, or instability. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Assume UTI is the cause and request antibiotics immediately
Assess for other causes of delirium and monitor while reviewing the full clinical picture
Ignore the confusion because the culture is positive
Diagnose pyelonephritis without further assessment
questions.explanation: Bacteriuria alone does not establish the cause of delirium. Without localizing or systemic infection signs, assess other causes and observe rather than reflexively treating asymptomatic bacteriuria.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: A urine culture is ordered for a client with an indwelling catheter and compatible symptoms. From where should the RN obtain the specimen?
choices: The drainage bag after it has been hanging overnight
The disinfected catheter sampling port using the local protocol
The floor beneath the drainage bag
The catheter tubing after disconnecting the closed system without indication
questions.explanation: A specimen from the disinfected sampling port preserves the closed system and reduces contamination; urine from the collection bag is not appropriate for culture.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: A client with a known ureteral stone develops fever, flank pain, hypotension, and reduced urine output. What is the highest-priority concern?
choices: Infected urinary obstruction with sepsis risk
Uncomplicated asymptomatic bacteriuria
Normal stone passage that requires no reassessment
Isolated bladder spasm without infection
questions.explanation: Fever and shock physiology in the setting of possible obstruction raise concern for an infected blocked collecting system. This needs urgent sepsis care and urologic source-control evaluation.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Why are antibiotics alone often insufficient for an obstructed, infected kidney?
choices: The infection requires relief of the blocked drainage system as source control
Antibiotics cannot reach the bloodstream
A positive urine test always requires stone removal immediately
The obstruction automatically resolves after one antibiotic dose
questions.explanation: An infected obstructed collecting system may need urgent decompression by a urologist, commonly via stent or nephrostomy, alongside antimicrobial and sepsis treatment.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which plan best reduces catheter-associated UTI risk?
choices: Keep every catheter until discharge for convenience
Use catheters only when indicated, maintain a closed system, and remove them promptly when no longer needed
Disconnect the drainage tubing routinely to inspect the urine
Collect a urine culture daily from every catheterized client
questions.explanation: Appropriate catheter use, aseptic insertion, closed drainage, and prompt removal are core CAUTI-prevention measures; routine disconnection and unnecessary cultures increase risk.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which finding most strongly suggests acute urinary retention?
choices: A strong urge to void, painful suprapubic distention, and inability to pass urine
Clear urine in a freely draining catheter
An isolated positive urine culture without symptoms
An unchanged baseline pattern of nocturia
questions.explanation: Acute retention commonly presents with inability to urinate and painful lower-abdominal or suprapubic distention. Assess promptly and use a bladder scan when indicated.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: A client treated for pyelonephritis remains febrile with worsening flank pain after starting therapy. What is the best next step?
choices: Assume the regimen must be working because antibiotics were given
Promptly reassess for resistant organisms, obstruction, abscess, sepsis, or another diagnosis
Stop recording vital signs until culture is final
Reassure the client that worsening is always expected
questions.explanation: Deterioration or failure to improve requires clinical reassessment and review of culture, source control, drug exposure, and other possible diagnoses.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which discharge handoff best supports safe follow-up after a complicated UTI?
choices: Report only that the urine looks clearer
Include symptoms and vital-sign trend, cultures and pending results, antibiotic review, kidney function, urine drainage, and source-control plan
Assume no follow-up is needed once fever falls once
Omit catheter and stent information because it is not medication related
questions.explanation: Safe transition requires a named plan for culture review, therapy adjustment, renal and symptom reassessment, and any catheter, stent, or other source-control needs.
